anomalies.observed: On the 'Water Level Sensor/Switches' sheet, R6 (10 k) is wired between +3V3 and the upper float line (J1 pin 2 = FLOAT_HIGH), and R9 (10 k) is wired between GND and the lower float line (J1 pin 3 = FLOAT_LOW). The float switches SW1/SW2 tie FLOAT_HIGH to VCC and FLOAT_LOW to GND, so with these pull assignments each float node is held at the same rail whether its switch is open or closed, and /BPUMP (reached from FLOAT_LOW through R2) is held low at power-up.
anomalies.expected: The specification's reference netlist maps the pulls the other way around: 'R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k' (and R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO). With R6 pulling FLOAT_LOW up and R9 pulling FLOAT_HIGH down, the switches can actually change the node levels and /BPUMP defaults high, keeping the main-pump MOSFET T2 off until commanded.

evidence.quote: Two float switches are read as binary_sensor GPIO inputs ... (with 10 kΩ/4.7 kΩ pull resistors visible in the .cir file: R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO 4.7k).
Sheet 1, 'Water Level Sensor/Switches': R6 10k from +3V3 to the FLOAT_HIGH net (J1 pin 2); R9 10k from GND to the FLOAT_LOW net (J1 pin 3).

anomalies.impact: Both float-switch inputs are dead (each node is stuck at one rail regardless of water level), so the firmware's low/high water-level binary sensors and the hardware pump/valve interlocks never see a transition. Because FLOAT_LOW is pulled to GND, /BPUMP is low, T1 is off and the R5 pull-up turns the main circulation pump (T2) ON at power-up, defeating the low-level dry-run cutoff.

anomalies.observed: On sheet 1 the LiDAR PR1 is wired through header H1: its SDA/SCL pins join the main I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL nets, and its TX pin (5) is tied to the EZO_PDIS net while RX (6) is tied to GND. EZO_PDIS is the single-wire power-disable control driven by ESP32 IO6 and connected to the PDIS pins of both ADM3260 isolators (U3.8, U4.8).
anomalies.expected: The specification states PR1 is not implemented in this design ('all four pins ... typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net'), and EZO_PDIS is intended to be driven solely by the MCU to power-cycle the pH/EC isolators. A sensor TX output must not be placed on that control net.

evidence.quote: the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no ... and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.
Sheet 1, 'Water Level Sensor/Switches': PR1 LiDAR pin 5 (TX) wired via H1 pin 5 to the EZO_PDIS net; pin 6 (RX) to GND.

anomalies.impact: The LiDAR's TX output fights the ESP32 driver on IO6 and the isolator PDIS pins, so the pH/EC isolated I2C bridges can be randomly enabled/disabled by the LiDAR's serial output, corrupting pH/EC sensing. (Lower confidence: depends on PR1 actually being populated in this build.)
